notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 12/16/2025
Patient: Ahmed Gerlach, 83-year-old male

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 12/16/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 32.0 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 15% of all events. These results indicate moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea. Recommendations include evaluation for positive airway pressure therapy and follow-up with sleep medicine specialist for management.

notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 07/25/2026
Patient: Ahmed Gerlach, 84-year-old male

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with CPAP therapy.

History:
Mr. Gerlach is an 84-year-old male with a diagnosis of OSA currently treated with CPAP. He reports consistent nightly use of his CPAP device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 33.8 kg/m2.

Assessment:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 25.5 events/hour on CPAP at 9 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options given CPAP failure.
2. Discuss potential for bilevel positive airway pressure or advanced therapies.
3. Recommend follow-up sleep study to assess efficacy of new interventions.
4. Continue monitoring adherence and symptoms.

Summary:
Mr. Gerlach demonstrates persistent moderate to severe OSA despite adherence to CPAP therapy. Further evaluation and treatment modification are warranted to improve sleep quality and reduce apnea events.
